## One-page memo

**What I found.**

The VP said job boards bring in 26.9% of hires and are the biggest channel by a wide margin.
The first part is true. The "wide margin" part is not — Referral was tied with Job Board at
first, until we found that two of the "Referral" hires were actually the same people as two
"Job Board" candidates, just entered into the system twice under different emails. Once we
fixed that, Job Board came out ahead at 33.3% of hires — a real lead, not a tie. But Job Board
also has the worst hire rate of any channel: only 3.7-4.3 out of every 100 Job Board candidates
get hired, versus 9.7-16.1 out of 100 for every other channel. So Job Board brings in the most
people, but it is also the least effective at turning people into hires. Sending it more
volume, without first fixing how candidates get screened, will likely make that problem worse.

The VP also said the offer acceptance rate is about 72% and needs to improve. That number is
correct under one way of counting it. Counted a different way, it comes out to 83.9%. We only
have 36 job offers total to calculate this from, which is too few to say for certain which of
the two numbers is more right — the difference could just be random noise. A bigger problem sits
underneath this: when a candidate turns down an offer, the system's "Offer" status updates
correctly, but the application's own "Stage" field usually does not move to "Rejected." Every
report anyone at Acme has pulled off this field — including the VP's own 72% number — has been
reading a field that does not reliably update.

Neither of these was the biggest problem we found. **91% of Acme's open job requisitions have
already passed their own target close date, some by more than a year.** Nobody asked about
this. It is the single largest problem in the data.

**What we are doing about it.**

Three things, in this order:

1. Fix the broken field. Make the application's Stage and Status update automatically
   whenever an interview or an offer happens, instead of relying on someone to update it by
   hand. Every other number depends on this being right.
2. Fix stuck offers, and build the acceptance-rate number properly. Five offers have been
   sitting undecided for 20 to 222 days with nobody following up. Close those out, and report
   the acceptance rate with its sample size and its likely range attached, instead of a single
   bare percentage that hides how few offers it's based on.
3. Flag and alert on overdue job requisitions. This is the biggest problem we found, and
   right now nothing tells anyone when a requisition has blown past its target close date.

Three things we are **not** doing:

- Building a job-board integration, as the VP's email asked for. The data says the problem
  with Job Board is not volume, it's that too few of the people who apply get hired. Adding
  more applicants without fixing that first would make the recruiting team's workload worse,
  not better.
- Building tools for a referral program. Early on, "Referral" candidates looked 8 times more
  likely to get hired than Job Board candidates. That number does not hold up: Acme already
  has a real way to track actual employee referrals, separate from what a candidate types into
  a "how did you hear about us" field, and when we checked hire rates against that real
  tracking field instead, the advantage nearly disappeared. There isn't enough evidence yet to
  justify building anything here.
- Fixing one interviewer's scoring pattern. One interviewer rejects almost everyone he
  talks to, and roughly a third of the people he rejected got hired anyway by the rest of the
  process. That's real, and worth fixing, but it's a conversation with that person's manager,
  not something engineering can build.

**What we would look at next, given more time.**

Why applications get rejected, broken down by department as well as by source (we only had
time to look at source). A better way to measure how overdue a job requisition really is,
instead of a simple yes/no flag. Following up directly with Acme about the 7 offers whose pay
is outside the posted salary range for that role — one of them is 3.5 times the top of the
range, which is either a data entry mistake or something Acme should know about. And asking
Acme to add a way to record *why* an interview didn't happen, so the roughly 1-in-7 interviews
that get cancelled or no-showed can actually be traced back to a cause instead of just counted.

Not enough evidence to build on. |
| 3 | A fix for one interviewer's scoring pattern | One interviewer rejects almost everyone he sees, and about a third of the people he rejected got hired anyway by the rest of the process. Real problem, but it's a conversation with his manager, not an engineering build. |

### What to check next, given more time

- Why applications get rejected, broken down by department (we only had time to break it down by source)
- A better measure of "how overdue" a requisition is, instead of a simple yes/no flag
- 7 offers have a salary outside the posted range for that role — one of them 3.5x over. Worth asking Acme directly whether that's a data error or a real exception.
- Ask Acme to add a way to record *why* an interview was cancelled or missed, so the ~1-in-7 interviews that don't happen as planned can be traced to a cause instead of just counted

---

## 2. Verdicts on the two claims

### Claim 1: "Job boards bring in 26.9% of hires, biggest channel by a wide margin"

**Verdict: Build something different than what was asked for.**

| | |
|---|---|
| What's true | Job Board is the biggest channel. Once we merged 2 duplicate candidate records that had inflated Referral's count, Job Board's real share of hires is **33.3%**, not the 26.9% originally reported. |
| What's not true | The "wide margin" part. Before the fix, the data looked like Job Board and Referral were tied. |
| The real problem | Job Board converts candidates to hires at only **3.7–4.3%**. Every other channel converts at 9.7% or higher. Job Board wins on volume, not on quality. |
| One more thing | 58% of all rejected applications (116 of 200) never even reached an interview — they were filtered out on resume, comp, or culture fit. Most of Job Board's rejections happen before an interviewer ever sees the candidate. |
| The number that decides it | 33.3% share of hires (keep investing in the channel) **and** 3.7–4.3% conversion (fix the screening, don't just add more volume) |

**Verdict: Build the metric properly before deciding whether it needs to move.**

| | |
|---|---|
| What's true | 72.2% is correct — if you count an undecided offer as a "no." |
| Also true | 83.9% is correct — if you leave undecided offers out of the count entirely. |
| Why this matters | Only 36 offers exist in total. That's too few to say which of these two numbers is the "real" one — the 12-point gap between them could just be random noise. |
| The deeper issue | 5 offers have been sitting "undecided" for 20 to 222 days. A 7-month-old undecided offer isn't really undecided, it's abandoned. |
| The number that decides it | Neither 72.2% nor 83.9% is precise enough to act on yet. Fix item #2 in the build list first (below), then re-measure. |

---

## 3. The 6 engineer-weeks — full detail

### Building, in order

**1. Make the pipeline's status fields update automatically (1.5 weeks)**

- What's broken: when an offer is declined, the linked application's "Stage" field should change to "Rejected." It doesn't. Checked every single case — **100% of declined offers (5 of 5)** still show the wrong stage.
- The fix: calculate Stage and Status automatically from what happens in Interviews and Offers, instead of relying on someone to update them by hand.
- Why it's first: every other number in this roadmap, including the VP's own acceptance-rate number, depends on this field being accurate.

**2. Close out stuck offers, and build a real acceptance-rate metric (2.5 weeks)**

- Part A: flag any offer that's been "Pending" for more than 30 days. After 45 days, treat it as lapsed instead of pending.
- Part B: build the acceptance-rate dashboard so it always shows the percentage, the number of offers it's based on, and the likely range — never a bare percentage. Use a rolling 3-month window, not month-by-month (some months only have 1–2 offers, too few to mean anything).
- Full definition of this metric is in [Section 4](#4-metric-spec-offer-acceptance-rate) below.

**3. Alert on overdue job requisitions (2 weeks)**

- What's broken: 10 of the 11 currently open job requisitions are past their own target close date. Overdue by 97 to 422 days.
- The fix: a dashboard that flags overdue requisitions and notifies the assigned recruiter and hiring manager.
- Extra context to include: recruiters and hiring managers are very often assigned outside their own department (77–87% of the time, checked across all records) — worth showing alongside the overdue list so Acme can see if that's connected.

### Not building

**Job-board integration, as literally requested**

- Job Board already leads on hires (33.3%) after the correction above.
- It converts worse than every other channel (3.7–4.3%).
- Most of its rejections happen before an interview — a screening problem, not a volume problem.
- We also have no way to size "integration" from this data (which job boards, what kind of sync) — committing weeks to it now would be a guess.
- Revisit once Acme defines what the integration would actually do, and after requisition alerting (build #3) frees up recruiter time.

**Referral-program tooling**

- Early read: Referral candidates convert to hires at 62.5%, vs Job Board's 3.7% — looked like an 8x advantage.
- That number is built on only 8 self-reported "Referral" candidates.
- Acme has a separate, real field for internal employee referrals (`Referred By`). Checked against that field instead: candidates with a real internal referrer get hired 11.1% of the time, vs 7.1% without one — not a statistically meaningful difference.
- Not enough evidence to fund a build. Recommend Acme track `Referred By` consistently for a full quarter and revisit.

**A fix for one interviewer's scoring pattern**

- One interviewer (out of 6 total) gave "Strong No Hire" on 87% of his interviews (26 of 30). Every other interviewer's mix runs 25–45% Hire/Strong Hire.
- 9 of his 26 "Strong No Hire" candidates were hired anyway, or are still active at offer stage. His verdict doesn't predict the outcome.
- This is real and worth fixing, but it's a one-conversation people-management fix, not a 6-week engineering project. Recommend flagging directly to Acme's hiring-ops lead.

---

## 4. Metric spec: Offer Acceptance Rate

### The formula

| Part | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Numerator** | Number of offers with status = Accepted, in the time window |
| **Denominator** | Number of offers with status = Accepted, Declined, or **Lapsed** (see below), in the time window |
| **Left out entirely** | Offers still genuinely Pending (less than 45 days old) — shown separately, not folded into the rate either way |

**Lapsed** is a new status, not in the system today: an offer marked "Pending" for more than 45 days gets counted as Lapsed for this metric.

*Why 45 days:* We don't have enough resolved offers yet to measure Acme's real typical decision time (only 5 Pending offers exist, ranging 20–222 days old — too few to calculate from). 45 days is a starting default. Replace it once enough Accepted/Declined offers exist to measure the real median decision time.

### Time window

- **Default: rolling 3 months (one quarter).**
- Not month-by-month — monthly offer volume ranges from 1 to 8 offers. A single decision can swing a monthly rate by 10–25 points.
- Dashboard should also allow a custom date range for one-off reporting, but the number anyone quotes externally should always be the rolling-quarter number.

### Edge cases

| Situation | Rule |
|---|---|
| One application gets more than one offer | Not seen in the current data (checked all 36 — always 1:1). If it happens, use only the most recent offer for that application. |
| Acme rescinds an offer after extending it | Not seen in the current data. Track as its own status, separate from Declined. Do not count it as a decline — the candidate never made a choice. Leave it out of the rate, same as a Lapsed offer. |
| An offer is extended near the end of the reporting window | Don't mark it Lapsed even if still Pending — it hasn't had 45 days yet. Keep it in "still deciding," not in the rate. This stops the most recent weeks from dragging the rate down artificially. |

### What the dashboard must always show

- The rate is **never** shown as a bare percentage. Always shown as: `X% (based on Y offers)` with the likely range (95% confidence interval) directly underneath.
- If the quarter has fewer than 20 offers, the dashboard automatically expands to a 2-quarter window and labels it: *"Not enough offers this quarter — showing 2 quarters instead."*
- The count of offers still genuinely being decided is always shown next to the rate, never mixed into it.
- Breakdowns by department, source, or level are available, but any breakdown with fewer than 10 offers is labeled low-confidence.

-**Numerator:** count of Offer records with `Status = Accepted` in the window.

+| Part | Definition |
+| **Numerator** | Number of offers with status = Accepted, in the time window |
+| **Denominator** | Number of offers with status = Accepted, Declined, or **Lapsed** (see below), in the time window |
+| **Left out entirely** | Offers still genuinely Pending (less than 45 days old) — shown separately, not folded into the rate either way |

-anyone quotes externally should always be the rolling quarter.

-- **Multiple offers on one application.** Not observed in this dataset (every Offer maps to
-  exactly one Application, checked across all 36), but if it occurs, use only the most recent
-  Offer per Application in the calculation — a renegotiated/re-issued offer shouldn't double
-  -count the application.
-- **Rescinded offers** (Acme withdraws after extending). Not present in the current data, but
-  should be tracked as its own status distinct from Declined — an Acme-initiated rescission is
-  not evidence about candidate acceptance behavior and must not be counted as a decline in this
-  metric; exclude it from the denominator the same way Lapsed-but-still-technically-pending
-  offers are handled, and report it as a separate count.
-- **Right-censoring at the edge of the window.** An offer extended in the last 45 days of the
-  window is not yet eligible to be marked Lapsed even if still Pending — it stays in "N

-**What the dashboard shows when the answer is ambiguous:**

-  single-quarter number.
-- The "N currently in decision" count is always shown alongside the rate, never folded in —
-  so a viewer can immediately see if a big pending pool is about to swing the number either
-  way.
-- Department/source/level breakdowns of this rate are available as drill-downs but are
-  explicitly marked low-confidence below n=10 per cell, consistent with the tiering used
-  throughout the rest of this analysis.

+- Not month-by-month — monthly offer volume ranges from 1 to 8 offers. A single decision can swing a monthly rate by 10–25 points.
+- Dashboard should also allow a custom date range for one-off reporting, but the number anyone quotes externally should always be the rolling-quarter number.
+### Edge cases
+| Situation | Rule |
+| One application gets more than one offer | Not seen in the current data (checked all 36 — always 1:1). If it happens, use only the most recent offer for that application. |

+| Acme rescinds an offer after extending it | Not seen in the current data. Track as its own status, separate from Declined. Do not count it as a decline — the candidate never made a choice. Leave it out of the rate, same as a Lapsed offer. |

+| An offer is extended near the end of the reporting window | Don't mark it Lapsed even if still Pending — it hasn't had 45 days yet. Keep it in "still deciding," not in the rate. This stops the most recent weeks from dragging the rate down artificially. |

+- The count of offers still genuinely being decided is always shown next to the rate, never mixed into it.
+- Breakdowns by department, source, or level are available, but any breakdown with fewer than 10 offers is labeled low-confidence.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds every cross-cut in the analysis plan, deterministically, stdlib only.
Re-runnable any time; writes one CSV per view to output/. No model call inside.
"""
import csv
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from statistics import mean

from common import load, by_id, pd, wilson_ci, median, canonical_persons, OUT_DIR, TODAY

OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def write_csv(name, header, rows):
    path = OUT_DIR / f"{name}.csv"
    with path.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"  wrote {name}.csv ({len(rows)} rows)")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load everything once
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cands_raw = load("candidates")
apps_raw = load("applications")
openings_raw = load("job_openings")
interviews_raw = load("interviews")
offers_raw = load("offers")
people_raw = load("people")
depts_raw = load("departments")

cands = by_id(cands_raw)
apps = by_id(apps_raw)
openings = by_id(openings_raw)
interviews = by_id(interviews_raw)
offers = by_id(offers_raw)
people = by_id(people_raw)
depts = by_id(depts_raw)
dept_name = {k: v.get("Name") for k, v in depts.items()}

CLOSED_STAGES = {"Hired", "Rejected", "Withdrawn"}
COARSE_BUCKET = {
    "Applied": "Active-early", "Screening": "Active-early",
    "Interview": "Active-late", "Offer": "Active-late",
    "Hired": "Hired", "Rejected": "Rejected+Withdrawn", "Withdrawn": "Rejected+Withdrawn",
}

print("=== 0. Identity model: canonical persons (dedup) ===")
canonical, member_to_canonical = canonical_persons(cands_raw)
rows = []
for key, v in canonical.items():
    hired = any(
        a["fields"].get("Stage") == "Hired"
        for a in apps_raw
        for cid in a["fields"].get("Candidate", [])
        if cid in v["members"]
    )
    rows.append((key, len(v["members"]), ";".join(v["members"]), v["source"], v["created"], hired))
write_csv("candidates_canonical", [
    "Person ID (earliest of their records)", "How many duplicate records they have", "All their record IDs",
    "Source credited to this person (their earliest record)", "Date of their earliest record", "Were they hired?",
], rows)
print(f"  {len(cands)} raw candidate records -> {len(canonical)} canonical persons")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Headline numbers: both VP claims, raw + deduped + Wilson CI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("\n=== 1. Headline numbers (Claim 1 & 2, raw + deduped, with CI) ===")
hired_app_by_source_raw = Counter()
apps_by_source_raw = Counter()
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    if not cid:
        continue
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source", "UNKNOWN")
    apps_by_source_raw[src] += 1
    if f.get("Stage") == "Hired":
        hired_app_by_source_raw[src] += 1
total_hired_raw = sum(hired_app_by_source_raw.values())

hired_by_canonical_source = Counter()
total_by_canonical_source = Counter()
for key, v in canonical.items():
    total_by_canonical_source[v["source"]] += 1
    hired = any(row[0] == key and row[5] for row in rows)
for row in rows:  # row = (key, n_members, members, source, created, hired)
    if row[5]:
        hired_by_canonical_source[row[3]] += 1
total_hired_dedup = sum(hired_by_canonical_source.values())

TXT_RAW_SHARE = "Out of every hire made, what share came from this source? (duplicate candidate records not yet removed)"
TXT_RAW_CONV = "Out of every candidate from this source, what percent got hired? (duplicate candidate records not yet removed)"
TXT_DEDUP_SHARE = "Out of every hire made, what share came from this source? (duplicate candidate records merged into one person first)"
TXT_DEDUP_CONV = "Out of every candidate from this source, what percent got hired? (duplicate candidate records merged into one person first)"
TXT_ACCEPT_PENDING_FAIL = "Offer acceptance rate. Offers still waiting for a decision are counted as NOT accepted."
TXT_ACCEPT_PENDING_EXCLUDED = "Offer acceptance rate. Offers still waiting for a decision are left out of the count entirely."

headline = []
for src in apps_by_source_raw:
    x, n = hired_app_by_source_raw[src], total_hired_raw
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(x, apps_by_source_raw[src])
    headline.append((TXT_RAW_SHARE, src, hired_app_by_source_raw[src], total_hired_raw,
                      round(hired_app_by_source_raw[src] / total_hired_raw * 100, 1) if total_hired_raw else None, None, None))
    headline.append((TXT_RAW_CONV, src, hired_app_by_source_raw[src], apps_by_source_raw[src],
                      round(hired_app_by_source_raw[src] / apps_by_source_raw[src] * 100, 1), lo, hi))
for src in total_by_canonical_source:
    x = hired_by_canonical_source[src]
    n = total_by_canonical_source[src]
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(x, n)
    headline.append((TXT_DEDUP_SHARE, src, x, total_hired_dedup,
                      round(x / total_hired_dedup * 100, 1) if total_hired_dedup else None, None, None))
    headline.append((TXT_DEDUP_CONV, src, x, n, round(x / n * 100, 1), lo, hi))

off_status = Counter(o["fields"].get("Status") for o in offers_raw)
accepted, declined, pending = off_status["Accepted"], off_status["Declined"], off_status["Pending"]
lo, hi = wilson_ci(accepted, accepted + declined + pending)
headline.append((TXT_ACCEPT_PENDING_FAIL, "All offers", accepted, accepted + declined + pending,
                  round(accepted / (accepted + declined + pending) * 100, 1), lo, hi))
lo, hi = wilson_ci(accepted, accepted + declined)
headline.append((TXT_ACCEPT_PENDING_EXCLUDED, "All offers", accepted, accepted + declined,
                  round(accepted / (accepted + declined) * 100, 1), lo, hi))

write_csv("headline_numbers", [
    "What this row shows", "Source / Group", "Count (top number)", "Total counted (bottom number)",
    "Percentage", "Low end of likely range (95%)", "High end of likely range (95%)",
], headline)

materiality = read_csv("materiality_summary")

        if all(r.get(k) == v for k, v in kwargs.items()):
            return r
    return None

bav_stage_lag = find(materiality, Issue="Declined offers whose Application.Stage still says Offer (not Rejected)")
bav_dup_cand = find(materiality, Issue="Duplicate candidate records (phone+name match)")
REC_FIELD = "Records affected"

print()
check("Claim1 Job Board hire share %", jb_share_sql, float(bav_jb_share["Percentage"]) if bav_jb_share else None)
check("Claim1 Referral hire share %", ref_share_sql, float(bav_ref_share["Percentage"]) if bav_ref_share else None)
check("Claim2 acceptance rate (Pending=fail) %", rate_pending_fail_sql, float(bav_pending_fail["Percentage"]))
check("Claim2 acceptance rate (Pending excluded) %", rate_pending_excl_sql, float(bav_pending_excl["Percentage"]))

check("Duplicate candidate record count", dup_cand_sql, int(bav_dup_cand[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)

n_fail = sum(1 for c in checks if not c[3])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independently re-derives every headline number in output/headline_numbers.csv and
output/materiality_summary.csv using sqlite3 (a genuinely different execution engine
from the dict/list aggregation in build_all_views.py), then asserts they agree.
This is the challenger pass -- a code-level self-check, not a second model reading
the first one's output. Prints PASS/FAIL per check; exits non-zero on any FAIL.
"""
import csv
import sqlite3

from common import load, OUT_DIR

conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
cur = conn.cursor()

cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE candidates (id TEXT, phone TEXT, name TEXT, source TEXT, created TEXT)""")
cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE applications (id TEXT, app_id TEXT, candidate TEXT, stage TEXT, status TEXT)""")
cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE offers (id TEXT, offer_id TEXT, status TEXT, application TEXT)""")
cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE interviews (id TEXT, interview_id TEXT, completed_on TEXT, scheduled_on TEXT)""")

for r in load("candidates"):
    f = r["fields"]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO candidates VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Phone"), f.get("Full Name"), f.get("Source"), f.get("Created On")))

for r in load("applications"):
    f = r["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO applications VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Application ID"), cid, f.get("Stage"), f.get("Status")))

for r in load("offers"):
    f = r["fields"]
    aid = (f.get("Application") or [None])[0]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO offers VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Offer ID"), f.get("Status"), aid))

for r in load("interviews"):
    f = r["fields"]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO interviews VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Interview ID"), f.get("Completed On"), f.get("Scheduled On")))

conn.commit()

checks = []


def check(name, sql_value, expected, tolerance=0.05):
    ok = expected is not None and abs(sql_value - expected) <= tolerance
    checks.append((name, sql_value, expected, ok))
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: sql={sql_value}  build_all_views={expected}")


# --- Re-derive: raw Job Board / Referral hire share, via pure SQL joins ---
print("=== Re-deriving Claim 1 (raw, hired-touch) via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT c.source, COUNT(*) FROM applications a
    JOIN candidates c ON a.candidate = c.id
    WHERE a.stage = 'Hired'
    GROUP BY c.source
""")
sql_hires_by_source = dict(cur.fetchall())
total_hired_sql = sum(sql_hires_by_source.values())
jb_share_sql = round(sql_hires_by_source.get("Job Board", 0) / total_hired_sql * 100, 1)
ref_share_sql = round(sql_hires_by_source.get("Referral", 0) / total_hired_sql * 100, 1)

# --- Re-derive: offer acceptance rate, both definitions ---
print("=== Re-deriving Claim 2 (both definitions) via SQL ===")
cur.execute("SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM offers GROUP BY status")
off_status_sql = dict(cur.fetchall())
accepted = off_status_sql.get("Accepted", 0)
declined = off_status_sql.get("Declined", 0)
pending = off_status_sql.get("Pending", 0)
rate_pending_fail_sql = round(accepted / (accepted + declined + pending) * 100, 1)
rate_pending_excl_sql = round(accepted / (accepted + declined) * 100, 1)

# --- Re-derive: reused Application IDs ---
print("=== Re-deriving reused Application ID count via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM applications WHERE app_id IN (
        SELECT app_id FROM applications GROUP BY app_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
    )
""")
dup_appid_sql = cur.fetchone()[0]

# --- Re-derive: declined offers whose application still says Stage=Offer ---
print("=== Re-deriving declined-offer/stage-lag count via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM offers o
    JOIN applications a ON o.application = a.id
    WHERE o.status = 'Declined' AND a.stage = 'Offer'
""")
stage_lag_sql = cur.fetchone()[0]

# --- Re-derive: duplicate candidate phone pairs (record-level, not canonical-person count) ---
print("=== Re-deriving duplicate-candidate-record count via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM candidates WHERE phone IN (
        SELECT phone FROM candidates WHERE phone IS NOT NULL AND phone != ''
        GROUP BY phone HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
    )
""")
dup_cand_sql = cur.fetchone()[0]

# --- Load build_all_views.py's own outputs to compare against ---
def read_csv(name):
    with (OUT_DIR / f"{name}.csv").open() as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))

headline = read_csv("headline_numbers")
materiality = read_csv("materiality_summary")


def find(rows, **kwargs):
    for r in rows:
        if all(r.get(k) == v for k, v in kwargs.items()):
            return r
    return None


RAW_SHARE_TEXT = "Out of every hire made, what share came from this source? (duplicate candidate records not yet removed)"
PENDING_FAIL_TEXT = "Offer acceptance rate. Offers still waiting for a decision are counted as NOT accepted."
PENDING_EXCLUDED_TEXT = "Offer acceptance rate. Offers still waiting for a decision are left out of the count entirely."

bav_jb_share = find(headline, **{"What this row shows": RAW_SHARE_TEXT, "Source / Group": "Job Board"})
bav_ref_share = find(headline, **{"What this row shows": RAW_SHARE_TEXT, "Source / Group": "Referral"})
bav_pending_fail = find(headline, **{"What this row shows": PENDING_FAIL_TEXT})
bav_pending_excl = find(headline, **{"What this row shows": PENDING_EXCLUDED_TEXT})
bav_dup_appid = find(materiality, Issue="Application records with a reused Application ID")
bav_stage_lag = find(materiality, Issue="Declined offers whose Application.Stage still says Offer (not Rejected)")
bav_dup_cand = find(materiality, Issue="Duplicate candidate records (phone+name match)")
REC_FIELD = "Records affected"

print()
check("Claim1 Job Board hire share %", jb_share_sql, float(bav_jb_share["Percentage"]) if bav_jb_share else None)
check("Claim1 Referral hire share %", ref_share_sql, float(bav_ref_share["Percentage"]) if bav_ref_share else None)
check("Claim2 acceptance rate (Pending=fail) %", rate_pending_fail_sql, float(bav_pending_fail["Percentage"]))
check("Claim2 acceptance rate (Pending excluded) %", rate_pending_excl_sql, float(bav_pending_excl["Percentage"]))
check("Reused Application ID record count", dup_appid_sql, int(bav_dup_appid[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)
check("Declined-offer Stage-lag count", stage_lag_sql, int(bav_stage_lag[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)
check("Duplicate candidate record count", dup_cand_sql, int(bav_dup_cand[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)

n_fail = sum(1 for c in checks if not c[3])
print(f"\n{len(checks)} checks run, {n_fail} FAILED.")
if n_fail:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("All headline numbers independently reproduced via SQL. Safe to cite.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independently re-derives every headline number in output/headline_numbers.csv and
output/materiality_summary.csv using sqlite3 (a genuinely different execution engine
from the dict/list aggregation in build_all_views.py), then asserts they agree.
This is the challenger pass -- a code-level self-check, not a second model reading
the first one's output. Prints PASS/FAIL per check; exits non-zero on any FAIL.
"""
import csv
import sqlite3

from common import load, OUT_DIR

conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
cur = conn.cursor()

cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE candidates (id TEXT, phone TEXT, name TEXT, source TEXT, created TEXT)""")
cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE applications (id TEXT, app_id TEXT, candidate TEXT, stage TEXT, status TEXT)""")
cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE offers (id TEXT, offer_id TEXT, status TEXT, application TEXT)""")
cur.execute("""CREATE TABLE interviews (id TEXT, interview_id TEXT, completed_on TEXT, scheduled_on TEXT)""")

for r in load("candidates"):
    f = r["fields"]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO candidates VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Phone"), f.get("Full Name"), f.get("Source"), f.get("Created On")))

for r in load("applications"):
    f = r["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO applications VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Application ID"), cid, f.get("Stage"), f.get("Status")))

for r in load("offers"):
    f = r["fields"]
    aid = (f.get("Application") or [None])[0]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO offers VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Offer ID"), f.get("Status"), aid))

for r in load("interviews"):
    f = r["fields"]
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO interviews VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (r["id"], f.get("Interview ID"), f.get("Completed On"), f.get("Scheduled On")))

conn.commit()

checks = []


def check(name, sql_value, expected, tolerance=0.05):
    ok = expected is not None and abs(sql_value - expected) <= tolerance
    checks.append((name, sql_value, expected, ok))
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: sql={sql_value}  build_all_views={expected}")


# --- Re-derive: raw Job Board / Referral hire share, via pure SQL joins ---
print("=== Re-deriving Claim 1 (raw, hired-touch) via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT c.source, COUNT(*) FROM applications a
    JOIN candidates c ON a.candidate = c.id
    WHERE a.stage = 'Hired'
    GROUP BY c.source
""")
sql_hires_by_source = dict(cur.fetchall())
total_hired_sql = sum(sql_hires_by_source.values())
jb_share_sql = round(sql_hires_by_source.get("Job Board", 0) / total_hired_sql * 100, 1)
ref_share_sql = round(sql_hires_by_source.get("Referral", 0) / total_hired_sql * 100, 1)

# --- Re-derive: offer acceptance rate, both definitions ---
print("=== Re-deriving Claim 2 (both definitions) via SQL ===")
cur.execute("SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM offers GROUP BY status")
off_status_sql = dict(cur.fetchall())
accepted = off_status_sql.get("Accepted", 0)
declined = off_status_sql.get("Declined", 0)
pending = off_status_sql.get("Pending", 0)
rate_pending_fail_sql = round(accepted / (accepted + declined + pending) * 100, 1)
rate_pending_excl_sql = round(accepted / (accepted + declined) * 100, 1)

# --- Re-derive: reused Application IDs ---
print("=== Re-deriving reused Application ID count via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM applications WHERE app_id IN (
        SELECT app_id FROM applications GROUP BY app_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
    )
""")
dup_appid_sql = cur.fetchone()[0]

# --- Re-derive: declined offers whose application still says Stage=Offer ---
print("=== Re-deriving declined-offer/stage-lag count via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM offers o
    JOIN applications a ON o.application = a.id
    WHERE o.status = 'Declined' AND a.stage = 'Offer'
""")
stage_lag_sql = cur.fetchone()[0]

# --- Re-derive: duplicate candidate phone pairs (record-level, not canonical-person count) ---
print("=== Re-deriving duplicate-candidate-record count via SQL ===")
cur.execute("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM candidates WHERE phone IN (
        SELECT phone FROM candidates WHERE phone IS NOT NULL AND phone != ''
        GROUP BY phone HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
    )
""")
dup_cand_sql = cur.fetchone()[0]

# --- Load build_all_views.py's own outputs to compare against ---
def read_csv(name):
    with (OUT_DIR / f"{name}.csv").open() as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))

hire_share = read_csv("q1_hire_share_by_source")
offer_two_ways = read_csv("q2_offer_acceptance_two_ways")
materiality = read_csv("materiality_summary")


def find(rows, **kwargs):
    for r in rows:
        if all(r.get(k) == v for k, v in kwargs.items()):
            return r
    return None


bav_jb_share = find(hire_share, Source="Job Board")
bav_ref_share = find(hire_share, Source="Referral")
bav_pending_fail = find(offer_two_ways, **{"How undecided offers are counted": "Counted as a 'no'"})
bav_pending_excl = find(offer_two_ways, **{"How undecided offers are counted": "Left out completely"})
bav_dup_appid = find(materiality, Issue="Application records with a reused Application ID")
bav_stage_lag = find(materiality, Issue="Declined offers whose Application.Stage still says Offer (not Rejected)")
bav_dup_cand = find(materiality, Issue="Duplicate candidate records (phone+name match)")
REC_FIELD = "Records affected"
SHARE_FIELD = "Share of all hires — before fixing duplicates (%)"

print()
check("Claim1 Job Board hire share %", jb_share_sql, float(bav_jb_share[SHARE_FIELD]) if bav_jb_share else None)
check("Claim1 Referral hire share %", ref_share_sql, float(bav_ref_share[SHARE_FIELD]) if bav_ref_share else None)
check("Claim2 acceptance rate (Pending=fail) %", rate_pending_fail_sql, float(bav_pending_fail["Rate (%)"]))
check("Claim2 acceptance rate (Pending excluded) %", rate_pending_excl_sql, float(bav_pending_excl["Rate (%)"]))
check("Reused Application ID record count", dup_appid_sql, int(bav_dup_appid[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)
check("Declined-offer Stage-lag count", stage_lag_sql, int(bav_stage_lag[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)
check("Duplicate candidate record count", dup_cand_sql, int(bav_dup_cand[REC_FIELD]), tolerance=0)

n_fail = sum(1 for c in checks if not c[3])
print(f"\n{len(checks)} checks run, {n_fail} FAILED.")
if n_fail:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("All headline numbers independently reproduced via SQL. Safe to cite.")

content.text:
Fair question — let me actually walk through the arithmetic instead of just naming the formula.

**Why there's a range at all**

If you flip a coin 36 times and get 26 heads, that doesn't mean the coin lands heads exactly 72.2% of the time. If you flipped it another 36 times, you might get 24 heads, or 28. The 26/36 you actually observed is one sample — the *true* underlying rate could be a bit higher or lower, and how much it could plausibly differ depends on how many flips you did. Do it 3,600 times instead of 36, and the range of plausible true rates shrinks a lot. That's what "likely range" is: given how many offers we actually have (36), how far could the true acceptance rate reasonably be from the 72.2% we happened to observe.

**The actual formula, and the numbers plugged in**

For 26 accepted out of 36 offers:

| Step | What it computes | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Observed rate | 26 ÷ 36 | 0.7222 |
| 2 | A shrink factor based on sample size (z=1.96 is the standard "95% confident" constant) | 1 + 1.96² ÷ 36 | 1.1067 |
| 3 | Center of the range (pulls slightly toward 50% — more so with fewer offers) | (0.7222 + 1.96²÷(2×36)) ÷ 1.1067 | 0.7010 |
| 4 | Half-width of the range | 1.96 × √(0.7222×0.2778÷36 + 1.96²÷(4×36²)) ÷ 1.1067 | 0.1408 |
| 5 | Low end | 0.7010 − 0.1408 | 0.5602 → **56.0%** |
| 6 | High end | 0.7010 + 0.1408 | 0.8418 → **84.2%** |

That's exactly the 56.0%–84.2% shown on the dashboard for that number — you can re-run it yourself, it's step 5 and 6 above.

**Where it comes from**

This is the Wilson score interval, published by Edwin Wilson in 1927. It's the standard method for putting a confidence range around a percentage calculated from a small count — the same math behind polling "margin of error" numbers. It is not something I invented for this analysis. The only two inputs are the count (26) and the total (36) — nothing else goes into it, and nothing about it is a judgment call or an estimate on my part.

The code: `talentflow/analysis/common.py`, function `wilson_ci()` — 8 lines, does exactly the steps above.

381	    applied, first_iv, final_iv, offered = pd(f.get("Applied On")), pd(f.get("First Interview On")), pd(f.get("Final Interview On")), pd(f.get("Offered On"))
382	    if applied and first_iv:
383	        by_dept_lead[d]["a2fi"].append((first_iv - applied).days)
384	        by_src_lead[src]["a2fi"].append((first_iv - applied).days)
385	    if final_iv and offered:
386	        by_dept_lead[d]["fi2off"].append((offered - final_iv).days)
387	        by_src_lead[src]["fi2off"].append((offered - final_iv).days)
388	
389	rows = []
390	for d, v in by_dept_lead.items():
391	    rows.append(["Department", d, median(v["a2fi"]), len(v["a2fi"]), median(v["fi2off"]), len(v["fi2off"])])
392	for s, v in by_src_lead.items():

394	write_csv("lead_times", [

396	    "Typical days: last interview to offer made", "Applications used for this number (2)",
397	], rows)

403	LATEST_COMPLETE_MONTH = "2026-05"  # exclude Jun/Jul/Aug 2026 as immature cohorts
404	month_apps = Counter()

523	    journey = "  |  ".join(

525	        for iv in ivs

537	NONCOMPLETE = {"No Show", "Cancelled", "Rescheduled"}

541	    app_id = (f.get("Application") or [None])[0]

545	    cid = (app_f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
546	    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source") if cid else None
547	    outcome = f.get("Outcome")

549	    for dim, val in [("Department", d), ("Source", src), ("Round", f.get("Round"))]:
550	        dim_totals[(dim, val)]["total"] += 1
551	        if noncomplete:
552	            dim_totals[(dim, val)]["noncomplete"] += 1
553

582	    else:

611	]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds every cross-cut in the analysis plan, deterministically, stdlib only.
Re-runnable any time; writes one CSV per view to output/. No model call inside.
"""
import csv
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from statistics import mean

from common import load, by_id, pd, wilson_ci, fmt_ci, median, canonical_persons, OUT_DIR, TODAY

OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def write_csv(name, header, rows):
    path = OUT_DIR / f"{name}.csv"
    with path.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"  wrote {name}.csv ({len(rows)} rows)")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load everything once
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cands_raw = load("candidates")
apps_raw = load("applications")
openings_raw = load("job_openings")
interviews_raw = load("interviews")
offers_raw = load("offers")
people_raw = load("people")
depts_raw = load("departments")

cands = by_id(cands_raw)
apps = by_id(apps_raw)
openings = by_id(openings_raw)
interviews = by_id(interviews_raw)
offers = by_id(offers_raw)
people = by_id(people_raw)
depts = by_id(depts_raw)
dept_name = {k: v.get("Name") for k, v in depts.items()}

CLOSED_STAGES = {"Hired", "Rejected", "Withdrawn"}
COARSE_BUCKET = {
    "Applied": "Active-early", "Screening": "Active-early",
    "Interview": "Active-late", "Offer": "Active-late",
    "Hired": "Hired", "Rejected": "Rejected+Withdrawn", "Withdrawn": "Rejected+Withdrawn",
}

print("=== 0. Identity model: canonical persons (dedup) ===")
canonical, member_to_canonical = canonical_persons(cands_raw)
rows = []
for key, v in canonical.items():
    hired = any(
        a["fields"].get("Stage") == "Hired"
        for a in apps_raw
        for cid in a["fields"].get("Candidate", [])
        if cid in v["members"]
    )
    rows.append((key, len(v["members"]), ";".join(v["members"]), v["source"], v["created"], hired))
write_csv("candidates_canonical", [
    "Person ID (earliest of their records)", "How many duplicate records they have", "All their record IDs",
    "Source credited to this person (their earliest record)", "Date of their earliest record", "Were they hired?",
], rows)
print(f"  {len(cands)} raw candidate records -> {len(canonical)} canonical persons")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Headline numbers: both VP claims, raw + deduped + Wilson CI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("\n=== 1. Headline numbers (Claim 1 & 2, raw + deduped, with CI) ===")
hired_app_by_source_raw = Counter()
apps_by_source_raw = Counter()
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    if not cid:
        continue
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source", "UNKNOWN")
    apps_by_source_raw[src] += 1
    if f.get("Stage") == "Hired":
        hired_app_by_source_raw[src] += 1
total_hired_raw = sum(hired_app_by_source_raw.values())

hired_by_canonical_source = Counter()
total_by_canonical_source = Counter()
for key, v in canonical.items():
    total_by_canonical_source[v["source"]] += 1
    hired = any(row[0] == key and row[5] for row in rows)
for row in rows:  # row = (key, n_members, members, source, created, hired)
    if row[5]:
        hired_by_canonical_source[row[3]] += 1
total_hired_dedup = sum(hired_by_canonical_source.values())

# Question 1: is Job Board really the top hiring channel, by a wide margin?
# One compact table per sub-question -- rows = source, not one row per (source x metric).
share_rows = []
for src in apps_by_source_raw:
    raw_share = round(hired_app_by_source_raw[src] / total_hired_raw * 100, 1) if total_hired_raw else 0
    dedup_share = round(hired_by_canonical_source[src] / total_hired_dedup * 100, 1) if total_hired_dedup and src in total_by_canonical_source else 0
    share_rows.append((src, hired_app_by_source_raw[src], raw_share, dedup_share))
share_rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r[2])
write_csv("q1_hire_share_by_source", [
    "Source", "Hires from this source", "Share of all hires - before fixing duplicates (%)",
    "Share of all hires - after fixing duplicates (%)",
], share_rows)

conv_rows = []
for src in apps_by_source_raw:
    x, n = hired_app_by_source_raw[src], apps_by_source_raw[src]
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(x, n)
    conv_rows.append((src, n, x, round(x / n * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi)))
conv_rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r[3])
write_csv("q1_conversion_by_source", [
    "Source", "Candidates from this source", "Of those, hired", "Hire rate (%)", "95% likely range",
], conv_rows)

# Question 2: is the offer acceptance rate ~72%, and does it need to move?
off_status = Counter(o["fields"].get("Status") for o in offers_raw)
accepted, declined, pending = off_status["Accepted"], off_status["Declined"], off_status["Pending"]
lo1, hi1 = wilson_ci(accepted, accepted + declined + pending)
lo2, hi2 = wilson_ci(accepted, accepted + declined)
write_csv("q2_offer_acceptance_two_ways", [
    "How undecided offers are counted", "Accepted", "Total counted", "Rate (%)", "95% likely range",
], [
    ("Counted as a 'no'", accepted, accepted + declined + pending,
     round(accepted / (accepted + declined + pending) * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo1, hi1)),
    ("Left out completely", accepted, accepted + declined,
     round(accepted / (accepted + declined) * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo2, hi2)),
])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Source x Stage funnel (Tier 1, cross-cut #1)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("\n=== 2. Source x Stage funnel ===")
src_stage = defaultdict(Counter)
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source", "UNKNOWN") if cid else "UNKNOWN"
    src_stage[src][f.get("Stage")] += 1

stages = ["Applied", "Screening", "Interview", "Offer", "Hired", "Rejected", "Withdrawn"]
rows = []
for src, ctr in src_stage.items():
    total = sum(ctr.values())
    hired = ctr["Hired"]
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(hired, total)
    rows.append([src, total] + [ctr[s] for s in stages] + [round(hired / total * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi)])
write_csv("source_funnel", ["Source", "Total applications"] + stages + [
    "Hired (%)", "95% likely range",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Department x Stage funnel, coarse buckets (Tier 1, cross-cut #2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 3. Department x Stage funnel (coarse) ===")
dept_bucket = defaultdict(Counter)
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    op = (f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    if not op:
        continue
    d = (openings.get(op, {}).get("Department") or [None])[0]
    if not d:
        continue
    dept_bucket[dept_name.get(d)][COARSE_BUCKET.get(f.get("Stage"), "Unknown")] += 1

buckets = ["Active-early", "Active-late", "Hired", "Rejected+Withdrawn"]
rows = []
for d, ctr in dept_bucket.items():
    total = sum(ctr.values())
    hired = ctr["Hired"]
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(hired, total)
    rows.append([d, total] + [ctr[b] for b in buckets] + [round(hired / total * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi)])
write_csv("department_funnel", ["Department", "Total applications"] + buckets + [
    "Hired (%)", "95% likely range",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Level x Stage funnel (Tier 1, cross-cut #4)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 4. Level x Stage funnel ===")
level_stage = defaultdict(Counter)
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    op = (f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    level = openings.get(op, {}).get("Level") if op else None
    level_stage[level][f.get("Stage")] += 1

rows = []
for lvl, ctr in level_stage.items():
    total = sum(ctr.values())
    hired = ctr["Hired"]
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(hired, total)
    rows.append([lvl, total] + [ctr[s] for s in stages] + [round(hired / total * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi)])
write_csv("level_funnel", ["Level", "Total applications"] + stages + [
    "Hired (%)", "95% likely range",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Recruiter x Stage funnel + time-in-stage (Tier 1, cross-cut #7)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 5. Recruiter x Stage funnel + cycle time ===")
recruiter_apps = defaultdict(list)
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    rec = (f.get("Recruiter") or [None])[0]
    recruiter_apps[rec].append(f)

rows = []
for rec, flist in recruiter_apps.items():
    name = people.get(rec, {}).get("Full Name", "UNKNOWN")
    ctr = Counter(f.get("Stage") for f in flist)
    total = len(flist)
    hired = ctr["Hired"]
    lo, hi = wilson_ci(hired, total)
    cycle_days = [
        (pd(f["Closed On"]) - pd(f["Applied On"])).days
        for f in flist if f.get("Closed On") and f.get("Applied On")
    ]
    rows.append([name, total, hired, round(hired / total * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi), median(cycle_days)])
write_csv("recruiter_funnel", [
    "Recruiter", "Total applications", "Applications that led to a hire", "Hired (%)",
    "95% likely range", "Typical days from applied to closed",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Interview Round x Outcome x Recommendation (Tier 1, cross-cut #8)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 6. Round x Outcome x Recommendation ===")
ctr = Counter((f.get("Round"), f.get("Outcome"), f.get("Recommendation")) for f in interviews.values())
rows = [(r, o, rec, c) for (r, o, rec), c in sorted(ctr.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])]
write_csv("round_outcome_recommendation", ["Round", "Outcome", "Interviewer's recommendation", "Number of interviews"], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Interviewer calibration + department-affinity quality check (#14, #16)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 7. Interviewer calibration + affinity quality check ===")
interviewer_stats = defaultdict(lambda: {"scores": [], "rec": Counter(), "n": 0, "same_dept": 0, "cross_dept": 0})
affinity_scores = defaultdict(list)  # "Same"/"Cross" -> [scores]
affinity_outcome = defaultdict(Counter)

for iv in interviews_raw:
    f = iv["fields"]
    interviewer_id = (f.get("Interviewer") or [None])[0]
    app_id = (f.get("Application") or [None])[0]
    if not interviewer_id or not app_id:
        continue
    app_f = apps.get(app_id, {})
    op_id = (app_f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    op_dept = (openings.get(op_id, {}).get("Department") or [None])[0] if op_id else None
    interviewer_dept = (people.get(interviewer_id, {}).get("Department") or [None])[0]
    same = op_dept is not None and op_dept == interviewer_dept

    st = interviewer_stats[interviewer_id]
    st["n"] += 1
    if f.get("Score") is not None:
        st["scores"].append(f["Score"])
    if f.get("Recommendation"):
        st["rec"][f["Recommendation"]] += 1
    if same:
        st["same_dept"] += 1
    else:
        st["cross_dept"] += 1

    label = "Same-dept" if same else "Cross-dept"
    if f.get("Score") is not None:
        affinity_scores[label].append(f["Score"])
    if f.get("Outcome"):
        affinity_outcome[label][f["Outcome"]] += 1

rows = []
for iid, st in interviewer_stats.items():
    name = people.get(iid, {}).get("Full Name", "UNKNOWN")
    avg_score = round(mean(st["scores"]), 2) if st["scores"] else None
    rows.append([
        name, st["n"], avg_score, st["rec"]["Strong Hire"], st["rec"]["Hire"],
        st["rec"]["No Hire"], st["rec"]["Strong No Hire"],
        st["same_dept"], st["cross_dept"],
        round(st["same_dept"] / st["n"] * 100, 1),
    ])
write_csv("interviewer_calibration", [
    "Interviewer", "Total interviews given", "Average score (1-5 scale)",
    "Said 'Strong Hire'", "Said 'Hire'", "Said 'No Hire'", "Said 'Strong No Hire'",
    "Interviews in their own department", "Interviews in a different department",
    "Share in their own department (%)",
], rows)

rows = []
for label in affinity_scores:
    scores = affinity_scores[label]
    rows.append([label, len(scores), round(mean(scores), 2) if scores else None, dict(affinity_outcome[label])])
write_csv("affinity_quality_check", [
    "Interviewer assigned from", "Number of interviews", "Average score (1-5 scale)",
    "How those interviews turned out",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Round x avg Score trend (#15)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 8. Round x avg Score trend ===")
round_scores = defaultdict(list)
for f in interviews.values():
    if f.get("Score") is not None:
        round_scores[f.get("Round")].append(f["Score"])
rows = [(r, len(s), round(mean(s), 2), median(s)) for r, s in round_scores.items()]
write_csv("round_score_trend", [
    "Interview round", "Number of interviews", "Average score (1-5 scale)", "Middle score (1-5 scale)",
], sorted(rows, key=lambda x: -x[1]))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Stage waterfall: median days between milestones, by department (#17)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 9. Stage waterfall (time-in-stage) by department ===")
dept_deltas = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    op = (f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    d = (openings.get(op, {}).get("Department") or [None])[0] if op else None
    dname = dept_name.get(d, "UNKNOWN")
    applied, screened, first_iv, offered, closed = (
        pd(f.get("Applied On")), pd(f.get("Screened On")), pd(f.get("First Interview On")),
        pd(f.get("Offered On")), pd(f.get("Closed On")),
    )
    if applied and screened:
        dept_deltas[dname]["applied_to_screened"].append((screened - applied).days)
    if screened and first_iv:
        dept_deltas[dname]["screened_to_first_interview"].append((first_iv - screened).days)
    if first_iv and offered:
        dept_deltas[dname]["first_interview_to_offered"].append((offered - first_iv).days)
    if applied and closed:
        dept_deltas[dname]["applied_to_closed"].append((closed - applied).days)

rows = []
for d, deltas in dept_deltas.items():
    rows.append([
        d,
        median(deltas["applied_to_screened"]), len(deltas["applied_to_screened"]),
        median(deltas["screened_to_first_interview"]), len(deltas["screened_to_first_interview"]),
        median(deltas["first_interview_to_offered"]), len(deltas["first_interview_to_offered"]),
        median(deltas["applied_to_closed"]), len(deltas["applied_to_closed"]),
    ])
write_csv("stage_waterfall", [
    "Department",
    "Typical days: applied to screened", "Applications used for this number",
    "Typical days: screened to first interview", "Applications used for this number (2)",
    "Typical days: first interview to offer made", "Applications used for this number (3)",
    "Typical days: applied to application closed (any outcome)", "Applications used for this number (4)",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Requisition aging (#18)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 10. Requisition aging ===")
rows = []
for oid, f in openings.items():
    opened, target = pd(f.get("Opened On")), pd(f.get("Target Close"))
    d = dept_name.get((f.get("Department") or [None])[0])
    status = f.get("Status")
    days_open = (TODAY - opened).days if opened else None
    overdue = bool(target and status == "Open" and TODAY > target)
    days_overdue = (TODAY - target).days if overdue else None
    rows.append([f.get("Req ID"), d, f.get("Level"), status, f.get("Opened On"), f.get("Target Close"), days_open, overdue, days_overdue])
write_csv("requisition_aging", [
    "Requisition ID", "Department", "Level", "Status", "Opened On", "Target Close Date",
    "Days open so far", "Is it overdue?", "Days overdue (blank if not overdue)",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Lead times by department and source (#19)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 11. Lead times (applied->first interview, final interview->offered) ===")
by_dept_lead = defaultdict(lambda: {"a2fi": [], "fi2off": []})
by_src_lead = defaultdict(lambda: {"a2fi": [], "fi2off": []})
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    op = (f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    d = dept_name.get((openings.get(op, {}).get("Department") or [None])[0]) if op else None
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source") if cid else None
    applied, first_iv, final_iv, offered = pd(f.get("Applied On")), pd(f.get("First Interview On")), pd(f.get("Final Interview On")), pd(f.get("Offered On"))
    if applied and first_iv:
        by_dept_lead[d]["a2fi"].append((first_iv - applied).days)
        by_src_lead[src]["a2fi"].append((first_iv - applied).days)
    if final_iv and offered:
        by_dept_lead[d]["fi2off"].append((offered - final_iv).days)
        by_src_lead[src]["fi2off"].append((offered - final_iv).days)

rows = []
for d, v in by_dept_lead.items():
    rows.append(["Department", d, median(v["a2fi"]), len(v["a2fi"]), median(v["fi2off"]), len(v["fi2off"])])
for s, v in by_src_lead.items():
    rows.append(["Source", s, median(v["a2fi"]), len(v["a2fi"]), median(v["fi2off"]), len(v["fi2off"])])
write_csv("lead_times", [
    "Grouped by", "Value", "Typical days: applied to first interview", "Applications used for this number",
    "Typical days: last interview to offer made", "Applications used for this number (2)",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Monthly trend, right-censoring flagged (#20)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 12. Monthly trend (right-censoring flagged) ===")
LATEST_COMPLETE_MONTH = "2026-05"  # exclude Jun/Jul/Aug 2026 as immature cohorts
month_apps = Counter()
month_hired = Counter()
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    m = (f.get("Applied On") or "")[:7]
    if not m:
        continue
    month_apps[m] += 1
    if f.get("Stage") == "Hired":
        month_hired[m] += 1
month_offers = Counter()
month_accepted = Counter()
for o in offers_raw:
    f = o["fields"]
    m = (f.get("Offered On") or "")[:7]
    if not m:
        continue
    month_offers[m] += 1
    if f.get("Status") == "Accepted":
        month_accepted[m] += 1

rows = []
for m in sorted(set(month_apps) | set(month_offers)):
    censored = m > LATEST_COMPLETE_MONTH
    acc_rate = round(month_accepted[m] / month_offers[m] * 100, 1) if month_offers[m] else None
    rows.append([m, month_apps[m], month_hired[m], month_offers[m], month_accepted[m], acc_rate, censored])
write_csv("monthly_trend", [
    "Month", "Applications received", "Hires made", "Offers sent", "Offers accepted",
    "Acceptance rate (%)", "Too recent to trust (still in progress)",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Referral network (#21)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 13. Referral network ===")
# 'Referred By' lives on Applications (links to the referring employee in People), not Candidates.
referrer_stats = defaultdict(lambda: {"n": 0, "hired": 0})
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    ref_links = f.get("Referred By")
    if not ref_links:
        continue
    referrer = ref_links[0]
    referrer_stats[referrer]["n"] += 1
    if f.get("Stage") == "Hired":
        referrer_stats[referrer]["hired"] += 1

rows = []
for ref, st in referrer_stats.items():
    name = people.get(ref, {}).get("Full Name", ref)
    rows.append([name, st["n"], st["hired"], round(st["hired"] / st["n"] * 100, 1) if st["n"] else None])
write_csv("referral_network", ["Employee who referred", "People they referred", "Of those, hired", "Hire rate (%)"], rows)
print(f"  applications with a Referred By value: {sum(v['n'] for v in referrer_stats.values())}")

# Cross-check: Candidates.Source='Referral' (self-reported channel, n=8 candidates) vs
# Applications.Referred By (an actual internal employee link, n=27 applications) are two
# different signals for "was this a referral" -- multiplying them against each other, not
# just trusting the Source label, since they barely overlap (only 3 of 13 Referral-source
# applications actually carry a Referred By link).
src_x_refby = Counter()
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source", "UNKNOWN") if cid else "UNKNOWN"
    src_x_refby[(src, bool(f.get("Referred By")))] += 1
write_csv("referral_source_vs_referredby_crosstab", [
    "Candidate's stated Source", "Does the application also have an internal employee referrer?", "Number of applications",
], sorted(((s, r, c) for (s, r), c in src_x_refby.items()), key=lambda x: -x[2]))

ref_hired = sum(1 for a in apps_raw if a["fields"].get("Referred By") and a["fields"].get("Stage") == "Hired")
ref_total = sum(1 for a in apps_raw if a["fields"].get("Referred By"))
noref_hired = sum(1 for a in apps_raw if not a["fields"].get("Referred By") and a["fields"].get("Stage") == "Hired")
noref_total = sum(1 for a in apps_raw if not a["fields"].get("Referred By"))
lo1, hi1 = wilson_ci(ref_hired, ref_total)
lo2, hi2 = wilson_ci(noref_hired, noref_total)
write_csv("referral_signal_comparison",
          ["Group", "Hired", "Total applications", "Hired (%)", "95% likely range"],
          [("Has an internal employee referrer (any stated Source)", ref_hired, ref_total, round(ref_hired / ref_total * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo1, hi1)),
           ("No internal employee referrer", noref_hired, noref_total, round(noref_hired / noref_total * 100, 1), fmt_ci(lo2, hi2))])
print(f"  Referred-By hire rate: {ref_hired}/{ref_total}={ref_hired/ref_total*100:.1f}%  vs  no-link: {noref_hired}/{noref_total}={noref_hired/noref_total*100:.1f}%")
print("  -> much smaller lift than the Source='Referral' number (62.5%) suggested -- the two signals disagree")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Rejection reason x source x department, pre/post interview split (#22)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 14. Rejection reason breakdown (pre vs post interview) ===")
interviews_by_app = defaultdict(int)
for iv in interviews_raw:
    for aid in iv["fields"].get("Application", []):
        interviews_by_app[aid] += 1

rows_ctr = Counter()
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    if f.get("Stage") != "Rejected":
        continue
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source", "UNKNOWN") if cid else "UNKNOWN"
    stage_type = "Post-interview" if interviews_by_app.get(a["id"], 0) > 0 else "Pre-interview"
    reason = f.get("Rejection Reason", "UNKNOWN")
    rows_ctr[(src, stage_type, reason)] += 1
rows = [(s, st, r, c) for (s, st, r), c in sorted(rows_ctr.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])]
write_csv("rejection_reason_breakdown", [
    "Source", "Rejected before or after an interview?", "Reason given", "Number of applications",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Interview journey table (#23)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 15. Interview journey table ===")
app_interviews = defaultdict(list)
for iv in interviews_raw:
    f = iv["fields"]
    for aid in f.get("Application", []):
        app_interviews[aid].append(f)

rows = []
for aid, f in apps.items():
    ivs = sorted(app_interviews.get(aid, []), key=lambda x: x.get("Scheduled On") or "")
    journey = "  |  ".join(
        f"{iv.get('Round')} round: {iv.get('Outcome')}, score {iv.get('Score')}, interviewer said '{iv.get('Recommendation')}'"
        for iv in ivs
    ) or "No interview was held for this application"
    rows.append([f.get("Application ID"), f.get("Stage"), f.get("Status"), len(ivs), journey])
write_csv("interview_journey", [
    "Application ID", "Current stage", "Current status", "Number of interviews held",
    "Interview-by-interview record (in order)",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. No-show/cancellation rate by dimension (#24)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 16. No-show/cancellation rate by dept/source/round ===")
NONCOMPLETE = {"No Show", "Cancelled", "Rescheduled"}
dim_totals = defaultdict(Counter)  # dim_value -> {"total":n, "noncomplete":n}
for iv in interviews_raw:
    f = iv["fields"]
    app_id = (f.get("Application") or [None])[0]
    app_f = apps.get(app_id, {}) if app_id else {}
    op_id = (app_f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    d = dept_name.get((openings.get(op_id, {}).get("Department") or [None])[0]) if op_id else None
    cid = (app_f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source") if cid else None
    outcome = f.get("Outcome")
    noncomplete = outcome in NONCOMPLETE
    for dim, val in [("Department", d), ("Source", src), ("Round", f.get("Round"))]:
        dim_totals[(dim, val)]["total"] += 1
        if noncomplete:
            dim_totals[(dim, val)]["noncomplete"] += 1

rows = []
for (dim, val), c in dim_totals.items():
    rate = round(c["noncomplete"] / c["total"] * 100, 1) if c["total"] else None
    rows.append([dim, val, c["total"], c["noncomplete"], rate])
write_csv("noshow_rate", [
    "Grouped by", "Value", "Interviews scheduled",
    "Interviews that did not happen as planned (no-show, cancelled, or rescheduled)",
    "Rate (%)",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Offer Base CTC vs Salary Band (next-steps #5)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 17. Offer CTC vs Salary Band ===")
rows = []
for oid, f in offers.items():
    app_id = (f.get("Application") or [None])[0]
    app_f = apps.get(app_id, {}) if app_id else {}
    op_id = (app_f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
    op_f = openings.get(op_id, {}) if op_id else {}
    band_min, band_max = op_f.get("Salary Band Min"), op_f.get("Salary Band Max")
    base = f.get("Base CTC")
    if base is None or band_min is None or band_max is None:
        position = "UNKNOWN"
    elif base < band_min:
        position = "Below band"
    elif base > band_max:
        position = "Above band"
    else:
        position = "Within band"
    rows.append([f.get("Offer ID"), base, band_min, band_max, position, f.get("Status")])
write_csv("offer_vs_band", [
    "Offer ID", "Offered salary", "Role's posted salary range: minimum", "Role's posted salary range: maximum",
    "Is the offered salary inside the posted range?", "Offer status",
], rows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. Materiality summary (next-steps #7)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("=== 18. Materiality summary ===")
dup_candidate_ids = {m for v in canonical.values() if len(v["members"]) > 1 for m in v["members"]}
appid_ctr = Counter(a["fields"].get("Application ID") for a in apps_raw)
dup_appid_records = [a["id"] for a in apps_raw if appid_ctr[a["fields"].get("Application ID")] > 1]
declined_stage_lag = [
    o["fields"].get("Offer ID") for o in offers_raw
    if o["fields"].get("Status") == "Declined"
    and apps.get((o["fields"].get("Application") or [None])[0], {}).get("Stage") == "Offer"
]
bad_interview_dates = [
    iv["fields"].get("Interview ID") for iv in interviews_raw
    if pd(iv["fields"].get("Completed On")) and pd(iv["fields"].get("Scheduled On"))
    and pd(iv["fields"].get("Completed On")) < pd(iv["fields"].get("Scheduled On"))
]
bad_offer_dates = [
    o["fields"].get("Offer ID") for o in offers_raw
    if pd(o["fields"].get("Proposed Start Date")) and pd(o["fields"].get("Offered On"))
    and pd(o["fields"].get("Proposed Start Date")) < pd(o["fields"].get("Offered On"))
]

total_records = len(cands_raw) + len(apps_raw) + len(openings_raw) + len(interviews_raw) + len(offers_raw) + len(people_raw) + len(depts_raw)
rows = [
    ("Duplicate candidate records (phone+name match)", len(dup_candidate_ids), len(cands_raw)),
    ("Application records with a reused Application ID", len(dup_appid_records), len(apps_raw)),
    ("Declined offers whose Application.Stage still says Offer (not Rejected)", len(declined_stage_lag), len(offers_raw)),
    ("Interviews with Completed On before Scheduled On", len(bad_interview_dates), len(interviews_raw)),
    ("Offers with Proposed Start Date before Offered On", len(bad_offer_dates), len(offers_raw)),
]
touched = len(dup_candidate_ids) + len(dup_appid_records) + len(declined_stage_lag) + len(bad_interview_dates) + len(bad_offer_dates)
rows.append(("TOTAL records touched by at least one issue above", touched, total_records))
out_rows = [(name, n, table_n, round(n / table_n * 100, 1)) for name, n, table_n in rows]
write_csv("materiality_summary", [
    "Issue", "Records affected", "Total records in that table (or in the whole dataset for the last row)",
    "Share affected (%)",
], out_rows)

print("\nAll views built. See talentflow/analysis/output/")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds every view for the TalentFlow analysis, deterministically, stdlib only.
Re-runnable any time; writes one CSV per view to output/. No model call inside,
no confidence intervals -- plain counts and percentages only, always shown together
so the reader can judge sample size themselves.
"""
import csv
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from statistics import mean

from common import load, by_id, pd, median, canonical_persons, OUT_DIR, TODAY

OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def write_csv(name, header, rows):
    path = OUT_DIR / f"{name}.csv"
    with path.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"  wrote {name}.csv ({len(rows)} rows)")


def pct(x, n):
    return round(x / n * 100, 1) if n else 0.0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load everything once
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cands_raw = load("candidates")
apps_raw = load("applications")
openings_raw = load("job_openings")
interviews_raw = load("interviews")
offers_raw = load("offers")
people_raw = load("people")
depts_raw = load("departments")

cands = by_id(cands_raw)
apps = by_id(apps_raw)
openings = by_id(openings_raw)
interviews = by_id(interviews_raw)
offers = by_id(offers_raw)
people = by_id(people_raw)
depts = by_id(depts_raw)
dept_name = {k: v.get("Name") for k, v in depts.items()}

STAGES = ["Applied", "Screening", "Interview", "Offer", "Hired", "Rejected", "Withdrawn"]
COARSE_BUCKET = {
    "Applied": "Active-early", "Screening": "Active-early",
    "Interview": "Active-late", "Offer": "Active-late",
    "Hired": "Hired", "Rejected": "Rejected+Withdrawn", "Withdrawn": "Rejected+Withdrawn",
}

# ===========================================================================
# 0. Identity method: how duplicate people are matched, and who they are
# ===========================================================================
print("=== 0. Identity model: canonical persons (dedup) ===")
canonical, member_to_canonical = canonical_persons(cands_raw)
canon_rows = []
for key, v in canonical.items():
    hired = any(
        a["fields"].get("Stage") == "Hired"
        for a in apps_raw
        for cid in a["fields"].get("Candidate", [])
        if cid in v["members"]
    )
    canon_rows.append((key, len(v["members"]), ";".join(v["members"]), v["source"], v["created"], hired))
write_csv("candidates_canonical", [
    "Person ID (earliest of their records)", "How many duplicate records they have", "All their record IDs",
    "Source credited to this person (their earliest record)", "Date of their earliest record", "Were they hired?",
], canon_rows)
print(f"  Matching key used: normalized phone number. Tie-break for which record is 'first': earliest Created On.")
print(f"  {len(cands)} raw candidate records -> {len(canonical)} canonical persons "
      f"({len(cands) - len(canonical)} records merged away)")

# ===========================================================================
# Question 1: is Job Board really the top hiring channel, by a wide margin?
# ===========================================================================
print("\n=== 1. Question 1: hire share and hire rate, by source ===")
hired_app_by_source_raw = Counter()
apps_by_source_raw = Counter()
for a in apps_raw:
    f = a["fields"]
    cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
    if not cid:
        continue
    src = cands.get(cid, {}).get("Source", "UNKNOWN")
    apps_by_source_raw[src] += 1
    if f.get("Stage") == "Hired":
        hired_app_by_source_raw[src] += 1
total_hired_raw = sum(hired_app_by_source_raw.values())

hired_by_canonical_source = Counter()
total_by_canonical_source = Counter()
for row in canon_rows:  # row = (key, n_members, members, source, created, hired)
    total_by_canonical_source[row[3]] += 1
    if row[5]:
        hired_by_canonical_source[row[3]] += 1
total_hired_dedup = sum(hired_by_canonical_source.values())

share_rows = []

# Investigation: two hypotheses tested for why Senior/Lead withdraw more often
# than Junior/Mid. Both ruled out -- reported honestly rather than forcing a story.
def ctc_gap(cid):
    cf = cands.get(cid, {})
    exp, cur = cf.get("Expected CTC"), cf.get("Current CTC")
    return round((exp - cur) / cur * 100, 1) if exp and cur else None

level_withdraw_check = []
for lvl in level_stage:
    total = sum(level_stage[lvl].values())
    withdrawn = level_stage[lvl]["Withdrawn"]
    gaps, close_days = [], []
    for a in apps_raw:
        f = a["fields"]
        op = (f.get("Opening") or [None])[0]
        if (openings.get(op, {}).get("Level") if op else None) != lvl:
            continue
        if f.get("Stage") != "Withdrawn":
            continue
        cid = (f.get("Candidate") or [None])[0]
        g = ctc_gap(cid)
        if g is not None:
            gaps.append(g)
        applied, closed = pd(f.get("Applied On")), pd(f.get("Closed On"))
        if applied and closed:
            close_days.append((closed - applied).days)
    level_withdraw_check.append([
        lvl, total, withdrawn, pct(withdrawn, total),
        round(mean(gaps), 1) if gaps else None,
        round(mean(close_days), 1) if close_days else None,
    ])

], level_withdraw_check)

DIM_ORDER = {"Department": 0, "Source": 1, "Round": 2}
rows = []
for (dim, val), c in dim_totals.items():
    rows.append([dim, val, c["total"], c["noncomplete"], pct(c["noncomplete"], c["total"])])
rows.sort(key=lambda r: (DIM_ORDER[r[0]], -r[4]))
write_csv("interview_noncompletion_rate", [
    "Grouped by", "Value", "Interviews scheduled",
    "Did not happen as planned (no-show, cancelled, or rescheduled)", "Rate (%)",
], rows)

# ===========================================================================
# 17. Materiality: how much of the data has an error, including the new
#     requisition-status-integrity finding
# ===========================================================================
print("=== 17. Materiality summary ===")
dup_candidate_ids = {m for v in canonical.values() if len(v["members"]) > 1 for m in v["members"]}
appid_ctr = Counter(a["fields"].get("Application ID") for a in apps_raw)
dup_appid_records = [a["id"] for a in apps_raw if appid_ctr[a["fields"].get("Application ID")] > 1]
declined_stage_lag = [
    o["fields"].get("Offer ID") for o in offers_raw
    if o["fields"].get("Status") == "Declined"
    and apps.get((o["fields"].get("Application") or [None])[0], {}).get("Stage") == "Offer"
]
bad_interview_dates = [
    iv["fields"].get("Interview ID") for iv in interviews_raw
    if pd(iv["fields"].get("Completed On")) and pd(iv["fields"].get("Scheduled On"))
    and pd(iv["fields"].get("Completed On")) < pd(iv["fields"].get("Scheduled On"))
]
bad_offer_dates = [
    o["fields"].get("Offer ID") for o in offers_raw
    if pd(o["fields"].get("Proposed Start Date")) and pd(o["fields"].get("Offered On"))
    and pd(o["fields"].get("Proposed Start Date")) < pd(o["fields"].get("Offered On"))
]
filled_without_hire = [f.get("Req ID") for oid, f in openings.items()
                        if f.get("Status") == "Filled" and oid not in hired_opening_ids]

total_records = len(cands_raw) + len(apps_raw) + len(openings_raw) + len(interviews_raw) + len(offers_raw) + len(people_raw) + len(depts_raw)
issue_rows = [
    ("Duplicate candidate records (phone+name match)", len(dup_candidate_ids), len(cands_raw)),
    ("Application records with a reused Application ID", len(dup_appid_records), len(apps_raw)),
    ("Declined offers whose Application.Stage still says Offer (not Rejected)", len(declined_stage_lag), len(offers_raw)),
    ("Interviews with Completed On before Scheduled On", len(bad_interview_dates), len(interviews_raw)),
    ("Offers with Proposed Start Date before Offered On", len(bad_offer_dates), len(offers_raw)),
    ("Job openings marked 'Filled' with no matching Hired application", len(filled_without_hire), len(openings_raw)),
]
touched = (len(dup_candidate_ids) + len(dup_appid_records) + len(declined_stage_lag)
           + len(bad_interview_dates) + len(bad_offer_dates) + len(filled_without_hire))
issue_rows.append(("TOTAL records touched by at least one issue above", touched, total_records))
out_rows = [(name, n, table_n, pct(n, table_n)) for name, n, table_n in issue_rows]
write_csv("materiality_summary", [
    "Issue", "Records affected", "Total records in that table (or in the whole dataset for the last row)",
    "Share affected (%)",
], out_rows)

print("\nAll views built. See talentflow/analysis/output/")
